Hi Elena / Digisonic InfoSec team,

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today — helpful conversation and great questions. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Recap / current status (short):
- SOC 2: formal engagement started; target to complete Type II audit in Q1 2027. We can provide a SOC 2 bridge summary and our list of compensating controls in the interim (attached).
- GDPR / HIPAA: Redwood Inference supports GDPR deletion requests and can sign a BAA for HIPAA-covered workloads.
- Data retention: default logs (api/ingest/trace) are retained 90 days; application-level backups are kept up to 180 days in managed snapshots.
- Deletion SLA: for live data we aim for 30 calendar days from a verified request; backups are on a 180-day retention lifecycle with an administrative process for removing data from snapshots on request (see details below).

Questions you raised we want to confirm next:
- Are immutable backups used for production snapshots and what is the immutability window?
- Restoration RTO for critical datasets (we provided typical numbers, want your target).
- Any specific vendor questionnaire items you want us to prioritize.

Attachments: SOC2-bridge-summary.pdf (interim controls & timeline).

Next steps proposed:
1) Please send us the vendor security questionnaire (or confirm attachment) — we’ll return a filled version within 3 business days.
2) Schedule a 45-minute technical deep-dive next week (platform security, backup flows, and deletion process).
3) If you need an interim evidence package for procurement (logs, control descriptions), we can share scoped artifacts under an NDA.

If that plan looks good I’ll send the questionnaire request and propose times.

Best,

Draft highlights / recommended language for questionnaire:
- Immutable backups: "Redwood uses periodic object-store snapshots with write-once snapshots for a 30-day immutability window by default; for customers requiring longer immutability we can enable storage-level WORM policies (90 days) upon contract." (Note: enabling WORM typically adds a small storage premium — call this out verbally.)
- Deletion from backups: "Our standard process is to remove live copies within 30 days of a verified erasure request. For backups, we retain snapshots for their configured retention (default 180 days). To honor GDPR erasure for data in backups we run a documented expunge workflow that marks objects and schedules them for removal during the next snapshot compaction window; this is a manual/controlled operation and we provide audit evidence upon request."
- SOC 2 interim evidence: attach SOC2-bridge-summary.pdf, control mapping spreadsheet (internal only — we can provide scoped artifacts under NDA).

Open items for commercial to confirm before reply:
1) Confirm willingness to enable 90-day WORM for Digisonic and whether we should list this as an opt-in add-on.
2) Finalize phrasing for deletion SLA that distinguishes live data vs. backup snapshots (I suggest: live data 30 calendar days; backups — retained per snapshot lifecycle, expunge-on-request with administrative compaction; expected complete removal within 180 days unless WORM prevents immediate purge).

If that language looks good I can finish the questionnaire answers and attach the filled doc for Marcus to send.

Thanks,

Elena / Digisonic team — thanks for the quick reply and for sharing the questionnaire. Attached: vendor_questionnaire_filled.docx (completed answers) and the SOC2-bridge-summary.pdf we discussed. Below are the concise answers to the high-priority items so they are easy to circulate.

1) Backups / immutability
- Default: production snapshots are created daily and retained for 180 days. Snapshots are administratively protected; by default we provide a 30-day immutability window on snapshot indices.
- Opt-in WORM: for customers that require longer immutability (e.g., 90 days), we offer a storage-level WORM option that can be enabled contractually. There is a small incremental storage fee for WORM policies.

2) Deletion / GDPR erasure from backups
- Live data: verified erasure requests processed within 30 calendar days (data removed from active stores).
- Backups: because snapshots are point-in-time, expunging specific objects requires a controlled compaction workflow. Our standard commitment: we will schedule the requested data for removal during the next compaction cycle and expect final removal within the backup retention period (up to 180 days) unless WORM is enabled. We provide audit logs and a deletion ticket showing the workflow steps; for customers needing sooner removal we recommend enabling the WORM opt-in and a tailored retention policy.

3) SOC 2 interim evidence
- Attached is the SOC2-bridge-summary with control mapping and our expected audit timeline (Type II, Q1 2027). We can provide scoped artifacts (runbooks, control evidence) under NDA; let us know the specific artifacts you need and we’ll pull them.

Next steps we propose: 
- Please review the attached filled questionnaire. If anything needs more depth, mark the question and we’ll expand the answer.
- Schedule the 45-minute technical deep-dive next week — suggested slots: Tue 12/1 10:00-10:45 PT or Wed 12/2 13:00-13:45 PT. Attendees we recommend: Marcus (AE), Grace (Security SE), our Platform Security lead (optional).
- If Digisonic requires the WORM 90-day option, we can surface pricing as an addendum and enable it ahead of signing.
